title.narrative: Institutional Review of Public Water Resources Management and Capacity Building for Reform

description.narrative: The purpose of the Grant is to assist the Federal Government of Nigeria to develop a reform program for rationalizing and restructuring water resources management institutions. The National Policy will contain broad guidelines for the establishing of an institutional arrangement which will ensure the most efficient performance of water resources management functions. The new water resources management law will include the required enabling legislation for the establishment or restructuring of water related institutions. The purpose of this project will be to undertake the analysis and audit for the restructuring of institutions at Federal, State, local and catchment levels. This will entail a process of detailed assessment of the current functions, authority, respons ibilities, human resources, budgeting, expenditure, activities and equipment of current institutions. The assessment will include an evaluation of the changes which would need to be made in order to ensure that the future institutions would be able to implement the National Water Policy and enforce the new Water Law. The principles of efficiency, professionalism, transparency, accountability and accessibility which will be entrenched in the structure and operation of a new institutional system will be assessed in the existing system. In addition, the purpose of the grant will also be to build the capacity of the Federal Ministry of Water Resources to undertake the reform program and implement the new policy and strategy, and to build the capacity of the Legislature to develop good law related to the management of water as a key natural resources which is currently under considerable stress. One of the most important aspects of the institutional reform program is the understanding that the program is addressing the working environment of many people, each of whom has different perspectives, varied potential, their own career objectives and the need for security. The institutional audit will need to be an inclusive process and will need to be undertaken very carefully, based on the fact that the human resources employed in the institutions are the most valuable asset of the institution. The process must be promoted as an opportunity for all and not a threat. The project forms a preparatory process which will enable both the staff of the Federal Ministry and key members of the Legislature to ensure that the best advantage is taken of the resources available during the detailed reform procedures of Policy development and the drafting are new legislation.
